2608.19611.title: Forking Fast: Efficiently Estimating Uncertainty Dynamics in Text Generation
2608.19611.paper_summary: LLM reasoning is stochastic, and so understanding a model requires grappling with the distribution of reasoning chains that it might produce for a given question, i.e., its uncertainty. Resampling-based analyses characterize this distribution, revealing which steps of a rollout determine how the model arrives at its answer. However, a major limitation of these approaches is that resampling text sequences at every token or sentence in a reasoning chain is very costly. Our work strives to make resampling analysis more computationally efficient, while also shedding light on an important scientific question: what is the right statistical model for explaining uncertainty dynamics in text generation? We show that when resampling many reasoning chains, uncertainty dynamics converge to stable patterns, and noise is largely an artifact of sampling rather than an LLM's sensitivity to each individual token or reasoning step. We develop a statistical model for smoothing noisy low-sample rollout data to better approximate high-sample data, allowing us to significantly cut sampling costs.
2608.19611.paper_summary_zh: LLM 推理是隨機的，因此理解一個模型需要處理它可能為特定問題產生的推理鏈的分佈，即它的不確定性。<lb/>基於重抽樣的分析特徵這種分佈，揭示了回放的哪些步驟決定了模型如何得出其答案。<lb/>然而，這些方法的一個主要限制是，在推理鏈的每個標記或句子上重抽樣文本序列的成本非常高。<lb/>我們的工作旨在使重抽樣分析在計算上更高效，同時也闡明一個重要的科學問題：什麼是解釋文本生成中不確定性動態的正確統計模型？<lb/>我們顯示，當重抽樣許多推理鏈時，不確定性動態會收斂到穩定的模式，而噪聲在很大程度上是抽樣的產物，而不是 LLM 對每個單獨標記或推理步驟的敏感性。<lb/>我們開發了一個統計模型，用於平滑噪聲低樣本回放數據，以更好地近似高樣本數據，從而顯著降低抽樣成本。
